the more similar the users are in the way they speak, the more they are friends and the more likely they are to follow and be followed by each other.
the more similar users are, the more they connect with each other, either in Twitter or in the real world.
the more similar the speeches of the users, the higher the homophily.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
users with similar political opinions are connected to each other in Twitter.
negative users, Trump supporters, and Hillary supporters have a strong homophily in Twitter.
the homophility among political users is higher than among non-political users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sentiment towards the candidates is an important factor to understand political homophily on Twitter.
the sentiment of the users’ speeches can define their political class, and the political homophily of the users in the same class is higher than the users in the other classes.
homophily is not exclusive for the same political party.
